title: tajemstvi z jednoho klice modulu Key
interface:
final class Drupal\api_csobrec\Service\KeyCredentials implements \Drupal\api_csobrec\Service\CredentialsInterface. Constructor (\Drupal\key\KeyRepositoryInterface $keys, \Drupal\Core\Config\ConfigFactoryInterface $configFactory, \Drupal\Core\Logger\LoggerChannelFactoryInterface $loggerFactory).

Every secret this module needs comes out of ONE key of the Key module: the Daktela address and token, and the address, port, login, password or private key of CSOB's SFTP. The key is of the type 'authentication_multivalue', whose value is a JSON object; its plugin declares fields = {} so any field names are allowed, and these are the ones this class reads BY NAME: daktela_url, daktela_token, sftp_host, sftp_port, sftp_uzivatel, sftp_heslo, sftp_klic.

STEP 1: keyId(): string
The id of the key out of api_csobrec.settings:klic, trimmed, '' when the setting is empty or not a string. It is returned even when no key of that id exists, because the status report has to be able to name the key nobody can find.

STEP 2: the values, read once per call from the key.
$this->keys->getKey(<the id>) returns a \Drupal\key\KeyInterface or NULL. NULL (and an empty id) means an empty array of values. Otherwise $key->getKeyValues() hands over the decoded JSON. Three things it can hand over that are NOT the expected object, and each of them means an empty array of values:
  - NULL, which is what the Key module returns for a value that is not valid JSON;
  - a list, which is what a key of some OTHER type returns: getKeyValues() wraps a plain value as element 0, and element 0 of a wrongly typed key is the whole secret. Reading only by the field names above is what keeps that secret out of every getter;
  - anything that is not an array.
Any \Throwable from the Key module (a provider whose file cannot be read throws) also means an empty array of values and is NOT rethrown: nothing of it may reach the morning run. What goes into the 'api_csobrec' log channel is the key's id and the exception's CLASS ($e::class), and its MESSAGE is deliberately dropped — a provider's message can carry the value or the path it was read from. What the operator gets besides that line is missing(), which names the fields, and a morning run that refuses to send anything without a token.

STEP 3: the getters. Every one of them reads its own field by name, casts a scalar to a string and trims it; a field that is absent, empty, an array or an object is ''.
  daktelaUrl(): the field daktela_url without a trailing slash (rtrim of '/'), because the client builds paths onto it.
  daktelaToken(): the field daktela_token.
  sftpHost(): the field sftp_host.
  sftpUser(): the field sftp_uzivatel.
  sftpPassword(): the field sftp_heslo.
  sftpPrivateKey(): the field sftp_klic — the private key in PEM, not a path to it. The whole string is trimmed, but what is inside it is untouched: a PEM without its line breaks cannot be loaded.
  sftpPort(): int. The field sftp_port, which JSON usually holds as a string; a value that is not a whole number between 1 and 65535 means 22. A missing port must never read as port 0.

STEP 4: missing(): array<int, string>
The names of the fields the hand-over cannot run without and does not have, IN THIS ORDER and with exactly these strings:
  'daktela_url' when daktelaUrl() is '',
  'daktela_token' when daktelaToken() is '',
  'sftp_host' when sftpHost() is '',
  'sftp_uzivatel' when sftpUser() is '',
  'sftp_heslo nebo sftp_klic' when sftpPassword() and sftpPrivateKey() are BOTH '' — one of the two is enough, and which of them is there is the operator's choice.
An empty array means everything needed is there. sftp_port is never named: it has a default. The returned strings are field NAMES; a value, or a part of one, must never get into them, because this list is printed in the status report, on the operator's terminal and in the log.

No caching of its own: the Key entity caches its own value, and a class that cached it would hold a secret in memory longer than the request that needed it.
notes: Vyzadal to programator Drupalu, ktery modul nasazuje: tajemstvi patri do modulu Key (typ Authentication (Multivalue)), vcetne adres a loginu k SFTP. Zadne tajemstvi uz necte ze settings.php. Pozor na dve veci, ktere jsou v kontraktu zamerne: getKeyValues() vraci NULL u nevalidniho JSONu a LIST u klice jineho typu (jeho prvek 0 je cele tajemstvi), a vyjimka z poskytovatele klice muze nest hodnotu, takze se nepreposila ani neloguje. Prvni pokus dilny se strazci na spolknutou vyjimku vyrovnal tak, ze pod PHPUNIT_RUNNING vyjimku pousteel dal (zadni dvirka pro testy, a navic mrtvy kod: tu promennou nic nenastavuje). Spravne reseni je zaznam do logu, ktery jmenuje klic a tridu chyby, ne jeji text.
